title: include! → mod: the fragments that modules still include (43 in 16 product files, 45 in 19 test files)
outcome: After the migration (master ebc30de9) src/main.rs includes no file, but 88 include!() of .rs files remain inside modules: 43 in 16 product files (persist.rs 17; workspace_watch, test_run_observations, engram_unadmitted_lifecycle and coordination_persist 3 each; persist_metadata_units, engram_unadmitted_closing and delegation_mcp 2 each; test_runs_api, test_run_waits, git, engram_source_roots, engram_named_root_reclamation, declared_run_observer, acceptance_source and acceptance_evidence_selection 1 each) and 45 in 19 files under src/tests. These are fragments of a module, not of the crate root: each shares its parent's private scope, so converting one means deciding what the parent and child see of each other (child module with `use super::*;` and visibility on what the parent reads, or leaving it a fragment where the shared private scope is the point, as with test fragments that reach a fixture's private state). `cargo fmt --check` does not reach an included file, which is the standing cost of leaving them. The conversion tool scripts/include-to-mod.mjs converts fragments of src/main.rs only; its header says it is removed with the last fragment, so this item also decides the tool's fate: extend it to nested fragments, or remove it and convert by hand. Filed on the coordinator's instruction (30a7a691 #54), unscheduled; he schedules it once Greg's pause lifts. Criteria are to be worded when it is scheduled.
acceptance: include! → mod: the fragments that modules still include (43 in 16 product files, 45 in 19 test files) is done
